title: agent-metrics/v1 payload envelope (common fields)
description: Validates the fields every agent-metrics/v1 payload must carry regardless of its kind-specific `schema` value (e.g. token-usage/v1). A kind-specific schema (see token-usage.schema.json) composes this via allOf and further constrains `data`. This document describes the JSON *payload* structure only -- the outer `<!-- agent-metrics:v1 payload_b64=... sha256=... -->` HTML-comment framing that carries this payload is text, not JSON, and is specified in docs/protocols/agent-metrics-v1.md section 2, not here.

schema.description: Kind identifier, e.g. "token-usage/v1". Payloads whose schema value is not recognized by a given harvester MUST be routed to that harvester's rejection log rather than partially interpreted (see protocol doc section 6).

upsert_key.description: am1_ + lowercase hex sha256 of the RFC 8785 JCS canonicalization of {schema, repository, subject}. See protocol doc section 5 for the exact recipe. A harvester MUST recompute this and reject the payload if it does not match the declared value -- the declared value is never trusted as-is.

emitter.description: Who produced this payload (provenance for debugging), not an authentication claim. Trust comes from the transport layer (protocol doc section 7), never from this field.

subject.description: What is being measured. Deliberately kept separate from `emitter` (who measured it) and `repository`/`change` (where it happened) so those three concerns are never conflated.

change.description: Optional: present when the subject was measured in the context of a specific change (e.g. a pull request). Not every subject has one.

data.description: Kind-specific payload body. Left unconstrained here; the kind's own schema (e.g. token-usage.schema.json) narrows this.
